To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
many of the noise interventions were associated with a change (increase or decrease) in the health outcomes, irrespective of the source, outcome and intervention type.

1) many transport noise interventions are effective in reducing health effects, but 2) the effect of interventions on health outcomes is not well understood because 3) the evidence is thinly spread across source type, outcome and intervention type, 4) the evidence is of low quality, and 5) further studies with better designs and analyses are needed to improve the evidence.
the evidence base for the effects of transport noise on human health is thin and the evidence base on the effects of transport interventions on human health is very thin.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the question of whether the noise reduction achieved through a transport noise intervention is sufficient to produce a health benefit, and the answer to this question is yes for most of the interventions.
the effects of interventions to reduce the impact of transport noise on health, rather than the effects of noise exposure per se.
the effects of noise interventions on health.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there are no studies that can provide a conclusive answer to the question of whether a specific intervention has an effect on health, but that there are studies that show that many transport noise interventions have an effect on human health.

there is sufficient evidence that transport noise interventions can be associated with a change of health outcomes and that the expected effect sizes can be estimated from exposure response functions.
the effects of noise on annoyance, sleep disturbance, and cognitive impairment of children can be reduced through interventions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the evidence base for the effects of transport noise on health is limited, and the evidence base for interventions to reduce transport noise effects on health is even more limited.
there was evidence of effectiveness of transport noise interventions for annoyance and sleep disturbance, and that the evidence was less clear for cognitive impairment of children.
there is a strong evidence base for the effects of road traffic interventions on annoyance, sleep disturbance, and cognitive impairment in children.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a large body of research on transport noise interventions and their effects on human health.

there is a need for a systematic and comprehensive review of the evidence of health impacts of transport noise interventions, and a better understanding of the effects of interventions on the exposure response functions.
there is a need for more research on the effects of noise interventions on health, especially on effects on cardiovascular diseases and cognitive impairment in children.
